content: Musashi homolog 1, also referred to as Musashi-1, is a protein in humans encoded by the MSI1 gene. This gene encodes a protein that contains two conserved tandem RNA recognition motifs. It functions as an RNA-binding protein involved in post-transcriptional gene editing. Musashi-1 serves as a stem cell marker and plays a critical role in regulating the balance between self-renewal and terminal differentiation of stem cells. Overexpression of the MSI1 gene has been linked to the malignancy grade and proliferative activity in gliomas and melanomas. MSI1 is highly expressed in neural progenitor cells and is essential for the normal development of the brain. A mutation in this gene is responsible for autosomal recessive primary microcephaly. Additionally, MSI1 interacts with the Zika virus genome, which may explain the heightened susceptibility of these cells to Zika virus infection.
